name: GLP-1 cycling / on-off

lead:
GLP-1 cycling describes using GLP-1 receptor agonist drugs, such as semaglutide, in on-and-off periods instead of continuously. People discuss it to reach a leaner body and to manage what happens when the drug stops.
Research cited by Wikipedia reports that people regain roughly half to two thirds of lost weight within a year of stopping these drugs. Studies of formal on-off schedules have not been described.

paras: In looksmaxxing and weight-loss communities, people describe a drug phase to lose fat, followed by a break, with lifting and protein intake used to protect muscle. Prescribing decisions belong to clinicians; this entry does not give dosing guidance.

Prescription-only drugs with gastrointestinal side effects. Reported concerns include weight regain after stopping, loss of lean mass in some studies, and cost as a leading reason people stop. Anyone on these drugs should follow their prescriber.

chain: Resistance training aims to preserve muscle
angle.text: The drugs themselves reduce weight, producing a leaner appearance. Cycling is a community strategy around stopping and restarting, not a tested regimen.

lead: GLP-1 cycling, sometimes called sema cycling after semaglutide, is the pattern of using GLP-1 receptor agonist drugs in on and off periods. People interested in appearance discuss it as a way to lose fat for a leaner, more defined look and then maintain it.

Real-world stopping is common. Wikipedia reports that cost was the main reason for discontinuation in the United States, cited by 48.6% of people who quit, and that weekly injections are another barrier.[1] Studies summarized there report that people regain roughly 50 to 70 percent of lost weight within a year of stopping, with some returning to prior weight in about 18 months.[1]

A 2024 systematic review cited on Wikipedia's semaglutide page found that lean body mass fell significantly in some studies on these drugs, though the lean-to-total mass ratio rose in all of them.[2] Because of this, community discussion often pairs the drugs with resistance training and protein.

paras: GLP-1 receptor agonists are prescription drugs for diabetes and obesity. Cycling refers to alternating periods of use and non-use rather than continuous therapy.

Wikipedia summarises studies finding that people regain about half to two thirds of lost weight within a year of stopping this drug class.[1] Semaglutide's article cites a 2025 systematic review reporting about 67 percent regained within the following year.[2]
A 2024 systematic review of six studies, as reported in Wikipedia, found lean mass unchanged in some and significantly reduced (up to 40 percent of weight lost) in others.[2]
Trials of continuous use and of discontinuation exist and are summarized above.[1][2] No study found tests a planned on-off cycling schedule.
